narrative: Material PL1__MB6ADE36 exhibits smooth, normally distributed demand averaging 13,268.6 units per working day (CV=0.14), with no statistically significant trend over the 113-day observation window. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.45, mean=2.50 days), making them the dominant driver of buffer requirements. A classical (r,Q) EOQ policy with normal-approximation safety stock is recommended: order 88,670 units whenever inventory falls to the reorder point of 57,982 units, maintaining a safety stock of 24,814 units to achieve the 95% service level target. This policy reduces estimated annual inventory costs by 60% versus the current SAP baseline (MOQ-only ordering, zero safety stock) while keeping peak inventory at 113,484 units — well within the 161,789-unit storage cap.

research_insights.selected_model: EOQ with Safety Stock (Normal Approximation) — (r,Q) policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and continuous (CV=0.14, 100% non-zero fill rate) with a normal distribution, making the classical (r,Q) EOQ framework directly applicable. The normal approximation for the safety buffer is valid and efficient for this demand profile. MOQ=14,098 is well below the EOQ of 88,670, so MOQ does not constrain the solution.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Low — peak inventory (SS+OQ = 113,484 units) occupies only 70.1% of the 161,789-unit storage capacity. No capacity constraint binds. If demand grows by more than ~43% the cap would become active.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ + Safety Stock = 38,912 units, which is well below max_storage_units. No infeasibility detected.
